description: The lawyer suing rapper Afroman for allegedly defaming Ohio sheriff's officials who raided his property finished questioning him today by asking him if there's "anything that could change your mind about what you're doing to these deputies?" "Is there anything that can change my mind about the fact that they shouldn't have been at my house in the first place? Is there anything that can change my mind about how my money shouldn't have been touched in the first place? No," Afroman, legal name Joseph Edgar Foreman, told plaintiffs' attorney Robert A. Klinger. "That's all the questions I have. Thank you," Klinger said."You're welcome," Afroman said. Afroman's lawyer is expected to call him as a witness in his case in chief this week at the Adams County Courthouse in West Union, Ohio. Trial began Monday in the lawsuit, which alleges Afroman defamed and put sheriff's deputies in a false light by repeatedly lampooning them after they searched his property in 2022. Afroman was never charged with a crime, and he ridiculed the raid in social media posts and in the music video to his hit song "Lemon Pound Cake." He's suggested one deputy is a pedophile and said he had sex with another's wife. He testified today that the sheriff's officials "never should have came to my house in the first place." "Fact, if they hadn't came to my house, they wouldn't have put themselves on the video camera and in my music career. All of this is their fact. All of this is their fault, and they have ... the audacity to sue me," he said. "So what they did, searching your house, gave you the right to do everything you —" Klinger said as Afroman cut him off. "Under the circumstance that I got freedom of speech after they run around my house with guns and kick down my door. I got the right to kick a can in my backyard, use my freedom of speech, turn my bad times into a good time. Yes, I do, and I think I'm a sport for doing so, because I don't go to their house, kick down their doors, flip them off on their surveillance cameras, then try to play the victim and sue them," Afroman said. You can watch more of Afroman's testimony here @Meghann Cuniff, here @Meghann Cuniff and here @Meghann Cuniff. #law #rap #police

description: A prediction-market company, Kalshi, is facing a lawsuit after refusing to pay out $54 million to users who bet on the fate of Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei. Traders had placed bets on whether Khamenei would leave office before March 1, 2026. When he eventually left power due to death, many bettors believed they had won and expected their payouts. But Kalshi refused to settle the bets, saying the contract had a “death carve-out” rule, meaning the outcome could not be decided by someone dying. Instead of paying the winnings, the platform voided the market and refunded some fees. Now a group of bettors has filed a class-action lawsuit, arguing the market wording said Khamenei leaving office “for any cause” should count — including death. They claim the company is avoiding paying millions after the outcome became clear. The case is now heading to court and could become a major test for the rules governing online prediction-market betting. description: Gold has just had its worst week since 1983, dropping 10.3% in US dollars. Silver got hit even harder, down 15.7%, while platinum actually held up the best, only falling 4.28%. The reason for the drop is a big shift in interest rate expectations. Earlier this year, the market was betting on rate cuts, which helped fuel that huge rally in gold and silver. Now that expectation has flipped, with markets starting to price in rates staying higher for longer, and maybe even going higher again. That change matters because oil has also ripped higher. If central banks were to cut rates while oil is pushing towards $100 USD a barrel, that would be massively inflationary, and that is the last thing policymakers want right now. The key takeaway for me is simple. This changes the short term picture, but not the long term one. The US debt is still unpayable, and even if we do get a period of higher rates from here, we saw in the 1970s that rising rates did not stop the precious metals bull market. Short term pain, long term thesis unchanged. Get your bullion from Liberty Bullion. What a time to be alive.

description: PT Summarecon Agung Tbk secara resmi menggelar Grand Opening Harris Hotel & Convention Serpong, Jumat (13/3/2026). Memiliki akses langsung dengan Summarecon Mall Serpong, kehadiran hotel ini akan menambah fasilitas terbaru, khususnya fasilitas penginapan dan MICE di kawasan Summarecon Serpong. Harris Hotel & Convention Serpong menghadirkan 282 kamar yang dirancang dengan suasana cerah dan kontemporer khas HARRIS, memberikan pengalaman menginap yang segar dan nyaman. Hotel ini juga memiliki fasilitas acara yang lengkap, termasuk 1 grand ballroom berkapasitas hingga 1.500 orang, 3 ballroom, dan 11 meeting room. President Director PT Summarecon Agung Tbk, Adrianto P. Adhi mengatakan, kehadiran Harris Hotel & Convention Serpong berperan sebagai infrastruktur pendukung aktivitas bisnis di Summarecon Serpong. "Hotel ini juga akan memperkuat positioning Summarecon Serpong sebagai Regional Hub, yaitu pusat aktivitas ekonomi, bisnis, dan pertemuan yang melayani kawasan Serpong dan wilayah sekitarnya,” terangnya. #summarecon #realestatid #summareconserpong #harrishotel #gadingserpong

Trump has won back the presidency but his approval rating have dropped since he returned to the Oval Office. According to the poll, 56% disapprove of his job performance so far, including 48% who strongly disapprove. As the government shutdown came to an end, 57% of Americans said lowering prices should be the top priority of the White House right now. description: In this week’s episode of my Style DNA podcast I had the privilege of interviewing the fashion designer and creative director Harris Reed... and I have to say I was blown away by his vision, his confidence, his charm and his down to earth warmth. Fighting for the beauty of fluidity, half-American, half-British Harris Reed designs to create conversation. Growing up with a strong sense of self, Harris was able to quickly understand the transformative power of clothing and its correlation with identity and liberation. While still studying at Central Saint Martins, he caught the attention of the likes of Harry Styles who he dressed in some iconic looks for his tour including his signature pussy bow blouses and flares. Alessandro Michele, the then creative director of Gucci, spotted him and recruited him to his design studio. His brand has gone from strength to strength showing Demi-Couture collections biannually in London and garnering VIP fans and clients including Beyoncé, Adele, and Sam Smith. The overall DNA of the Harris Reed brand and personal identity, is best described as Romanticism Gone Nonbinary. It puts the wearer and their fluidity - in whatever way it manifests, front and centre while staying true to the brand’s ethos that strives for a vision of gender fluidity and inclusivity. Personally, Harris dresses to invite the looks and stares, to blur the preconceived fault-lines people have about gender and sexuality. He is an incredibly striking and magnetic human being. In 2021 he was invited to dress Iman for the prestigious Met Gala... both he and Iman looked spectacular despite a little personal mishap on his way there...(too funny to write… you’ll have to listen!). In September 2022, aged just 26, he was appointed the youngest ever Creative Director of French fashion house @Nina Ricci. Harris is absolutely flying... and his recently published, beautifully illustrated book Fluid, is well worth a read… Thank you @Harris_reed for such an insightful and fun conversation xx Listen now!  #harrisreed #harrystyles #styleDNA #fashiondesigner #styleicon
profile_biography: Creative Director, Writer, Commentator, Podcast - Amanda Wakeley Style DNA

description: Polymarket is a strange problem of late-stage capitalism. It is a market that gets bet on, which ends up becoming its own sort of ‘poll of the market’. It’s all the worst parts of polling, plus all the worst parts of the stock market. It is very easy for a few agents to manipulate the markets with a few heavy bets. The ‘gambling’-ification of things is a wider trend that worries me, if for nothing else than the ease of those in charge to twist and turn the market. I am even worried that this fear is naive and that there is a bigger systemic issue in the way gambling is so imbued into our culture. Of course every transaction benefits a company. Of course the number of people who don’t win are so staggeringly low. There are so many people that as long as they keep their base big and they evangelize through memes and sponsorships (how many Draft Kings ads have you seen recently? Remember the Twitch scandal?), they’ll keep churning out profit at an insane rate. I wonder how many of these companies individually are sitting on enough money to change the lives of entire communities. I wonder how many could change the nation, and of the world. #gambling #politics #draftkings #polymarket #harris #zohranmamdani

description: My fellow Republicans, fellow patriots, fellow Americans who still believe in the promise of this great nation, We are eight months away from the most important midterm election of our lifetime—Tuesday, November 3, 2026. This isn’t just about seats in Congress. This is about whether we hold the line and keep America on the path to greatness—or watch radical left policies, runaway spending, open borders, and weakness abroad undo everything we’ve fought for. Right now, we have a Republican President in the White House, a Republican Senate, and a Republican House. Unified Republican government gave us historic tax cuts, energy independence, stronger borders, and a booming economy before. We’re delivering again—cracking down on illegal immigration, bringing jobs back, standing up to our enemies, and putting America First. But the left is fighting back hard. They’re desperate to flip the House, chip away at our Senate majority, and turn President Trump’s agenda into gridlock and chaos. Look at what’s happening: Inflation is still squeezing hardworking families. Prices for groceries, gas, and housing remain too high. The Democrats want to blame us, but we know the truth—their big-government spending sprees and green energy mandates fueled this mess. Our Republican majorities are fighting to cut wasteful spending, slash regulations, and unleash American energy so we can lower costs for everyone. Our southern border—after years of crisis—is finally seeing real enforcement. But if Democrats regain power, they’ll throw the doors open again, overwhelm our communities, strain our schools and hospitals, and reward lawlessness. We cannot let that happen. Abroad, our enemies are testing us. President Trump is projecting strength—standing with our allies, confronting threats from Iran, China, and beyond. Weak congressional majorities or a Democrat takeover would embolden them and tie the President’s hands. This election is about saving America from the socialist agenda that wants to: •  Raise your taxes to fund endless programs •  Defund law enforcement and let crime surge •  Erase our borders and flood our nation with unchecked migration •  Force extreme climate policies that kill jobs and drive up energy bills •  Weaken our military and apologize on the world stage We’ve seen what happens when Republicans stay home in midterms. In 2018, low turnout cost us the House and stalled progress. We can’t repeat that mistake. History shows the party in power faces headwinds—but we have the issues on our side: economy, security, freedom. And we have the leader: President Trump, who’s proven he wins when Republicans show up united. So here’s my call to every Republican in Cincinnati, across Ohio, and throughout this country: •  Vote Republican on November 3. Every single race matters—House, Senate, state offices. •  Make your plan today: Register if you haven’t, request your absentee ballot if needed, mark your calendar. •  Talk to your family, friends, neighbors, coworkers. Remind them: Your vote decides if we keep fighting for lower taxes, secure borders, safe streets, and American strength—or hand the gavel to the left. •  Get involved: Knock doors, make calls, donate, volunteer. One hour from you can turn an election. •  Bring someone with you to the polls. Turnout wins wars—and this is a war for America’s soul. We are the party of freedom, opportunity, law and order, and unapologetic American exceptionalism. We’ve got the momentum if we fight for it. President Trump needs a strong Congress to finish the job—draining the swamp, rebuilding our economy, securing our future. Don’t sit this one out. Don’t assume others will carry the load. You are the difference. When Republicans unite and show up in massive numbers, we win—and America wins. This November, let’s keep America First. Let’s protect what we’ve built. Let’s save our country for our children and grandchildren. Together, we will hold the House. We will hold the Senate. We will hold the line. God bless you, #fyp

description: Two traders disagree: one thinks an event has 80% odds, the other 60%. Common sense says the market should settle at 70 cents, right? WRONG. ❌ When both traders use Kelly betting (the mathematically optimal strategy of your utility function is logarithmic), equilibrium hits 75 cents - not the intuitive average. This isn't irrationality. It's pure math. Even perfectly rational traders create systematic bias because they're optimizing for risk-adjusted returns, not just expected value. The formula shows that extreme positions get amplified in the final price.  #predictionmarkets #kellycriterion #tradingmath #mathematicalfinance #tradingjourney

description: A new nationwide survey shows that Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, popularly known as Bobi Wine, is on track for a historic win in the 2026 Ugandan presidential elections. The poll, conducted by trusted Ugandan media, indicates that Bobi Wine could capture 60% of the vote, leaving incumbent President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni with just 30%. The survey was carried out between October 1 and 10, 2025, and involved a large sample of 20,613 Ugandans from all regions. It carries a margin of error of ±2.5 percentage points at a 95% confidence level. The findings clearly show a two-horse race, with other candidates sharing less than 10% of the projected vote. The poll highlights a remarkable shift in voter sentiment, especially in urban areas, where Bobi Wine’s popularity continues to grow. Kampala and Wakiso, long known as centers of political energy and activism, show strong support for his message of change and hope. His campaign promises to empower youth, create jobs, and fight corruption have deeply resonated with the younger population. In contrast, Museveni’s support remains largely in some rural areas, although the gap is steadily narrowing. The president’s appeal has long been based on development projects, infrastructure growth, and programs such as the Parish Development Model and Emyooga. However, many respondents said these efforts have not met their expectations. The survey shows Bobi Wine drawing strong backing not only from urban youth but also from rural voters seeking a new beginning. His emphasis on good governance, equal opportunity, and national unity appears to have won over millions who believe it is time for change after decades of the same leadership. While Museveni continues to promote peace and stability as his main achievements, these messages now seem less persuasive to many Ugandans who are struggling with rising costs of living and unemployment. Many say they want a leader who will address modern economic realities and involve ordinary citizens in decision-making. Regional analysis from the survey reveals Bobi Wine leading comfortably in Central, Eastern, and Northern regions, and performing strongly in the West. Museveni still holds some ground in parts of Western Uganda, but his dominance there has weakened compared to previous elections. The change in public opinion marks a major turning point in Uganda’s political landscape. Bobi Wine’s lead reflects the growing power of the youth vote and the urban middle class, who are now more engaged and determined to shape their country’s future. Political observers believe that if the current momentum continues, Uganda could witness its most competitive and transformative election in decades. The people’s desire for accountability, equality, and new leadership is shaping up to be the defining message of 2026. As the elections draw closer, excitement and hope are spreading across the country. The survey suggests that Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu is not only leading in numbers but also inspiring a movement for change, signaling a possible new chapter in Uganda’s history.

description: While Zohran Mamdani was running to be the next mayor of New York, he traded sharp verbal barbs with President Donald Trump. Mamdani once said that his administration would be “Donald Trump’s worst nightmare,” while Trump falsely accused  Mamdani of being in the country illegally and called him a “Communist Lunatic.” Now, after two Oval Office meetings with the president since he became mayor, Mamdani says the two men have a “productive relationship … that is also honest.” “The president and I have many disagreements. We're not shy about them,” he told PBS News Hour co-anchor Amna Nawaz in an exclusive interview airing Friday. “We've been public about them. We've been private about them.” One thing on which they’re “very much in agreement is a love of New York City,” Mamdani said. The mayor noted that during his second White House meeting with Trump in February, he asked the president for billions of dollars in federal grants for a major affordable housing project in Queens. Mamdani said he has also shared “my continued belief that ICE raids are cruel and inhumane, that they do nothing to advance the cause of public safety.” “I want to always be honest with the president and with the public about where those disagreements are, and also, that my job is not to litigate the disagreements, but to deliver for the people of New York City,” Mamdani said. When asked how often he and the president speak, the mayor said he “will keep that between the two of us.” #Mamdani #Trump #NewYorkCity #Politics #News

description: Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) on Tuesday touted the SAVE America Act, a GOP bill that would require ID and proof of citizenship to vote in federal elections, calling it a package of "commonsense" measures.   "If there's anything essential to the integrity of elections, it's ensuring that those who are registered to vote are eligible to vote, and that those who show up to vote at polling places are who they say they are," he said on the floor ahead of what is expected to be a dayslong marathon debate over the bill.   "And how do you do that? Well, by requiring that Americans show proof of citizenship when they register to vote — and that they show photo ID at polling places. That's what the SAVE America Act would do. It's just common sense."   The South Dakota Republican noted that photo ID is required in the U.S. for a host of other circumstances, like boarding a plane, visiting the doctor, getting a library card, renting a car and checking into a hotel room.   "But to hear Democrats talk, you'd think that demonstrating citizenship or showing a photo ID is an intolerable burden," he said. "Are they going to start boycotting libraries and airplanes and hotels for requiring a photo ID? Are they going to explain why they're perfectly justified in requiring photo ID for their political rallies, but why it's somehow an intolerable burden to ask people to show their photo ID when they go to vote? I expect they won't."   The bill is a top priority for President Trump, who has threatened not to sign any legislation until it gets to his desk, but Senate Republicans do not have the votes to overcome a Democratic filibuster, nor the votes to change the chamber's filibuster rules to approve it with a simple majority vote.   The president also wants to attach a handful of other provisions that could make it even harder to pass, including ending most mail-in voting, banning biological men from competing in women's sports, and prohibiting minors from getting transgender surgery. #johnthune #saveact #voting #cspan

description: 💭THINKING ABOUT: THE RISE OF PREDICTION MARKETS LIKE KALSHI AND POLYMARKET💭 and how they are symptomatic of our current relationship to critical thinking. We are so inundated with poor quality information that we’ve become reliant on intermediaries, be it ChatGPT or your favorite influencer, to process what is happening on our behalf. It’s no coincidence that in a moment where we are ceding a lot of that independent thinking, here comes a tool that makes the personal opinion the subject of the wager.  So many of our modern tools like generative AI treat reasoning as this vestigial intermediate step - only valuable insofar as it gets you to the correct answer. And the emergence of betting markets takes this idea to an extreme place via financial incentive. The natural outcome is speculation, because what use is there in understanding fundamentals and deducing outcomes if you can still get the coin toss wrong? Let’s talk about the problem with valuing outcomes alone and not reasoning behind them. #culturalanalysis #predictionmarkets #kalshi #polymarket #criticalthinking

description: 🔥 ICE (sí, la dueña de la Bolsa de Nueva York) acaba de invertir $2,000 millones en una app que te paga por adivinar el futuro… 👉 Se llama Polymarket, y así funciona: 🎯 Es una plataforma donde puedes apostar sobre eventos reales: – ¿Quién ganará las elecciones? – ¿Cuándo caerá la inflación? – ¿Cuántos tweets pondrá Elon Musk esta semana? Sí, literal. 💸 No funciona como una casa de apuestas clásica. Las probabilidades no las fija un casino, se forman con la oferta y demanda del mercado. Compras acciones entre $0 y $1 dependiendo de cuán probable sea ese resultado. Si aciertas, te pagan $1. ✅ Ganas la diferencia entre lo que pagaste y ese dólar. ✅ Pierdes si te equivocas. ✅ Ellos ganan el 2% de las ganancias. 💡 Lo más potente es que Polymarket no es solo apuestas... es un nuevo tipo de mercado financiero donde lo que cotiza son las probabilidades. Y ahora, con el respaldo de Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), que controla la Bolsa de Nueva York, su valor ya supera los $8,000 millones 🚀 📲 Polymarket funciona con criptomonedas y está marcando un antes y después en el mundo de las finanzas descentralizadas. #Polymarket #BolsaDeValores #ICE #Criptomonedas

description: A empresa que transformou qualquer evento do mundo real em um ativo negociável — de inflação a futebol — acaba de criar a nova bilionária self-made mais jovem do planeta. E sim… ela é brasileira. 🇧🇷 A Kalshi é uma exchange regulada nos EUA que permite negociar contratos de “sim ou não” sobre acontecimentos reais. Se o evento acontece, você ganha. Se não acontece, perde. Simples. Poderoso. Revolucionário. É a primeira vez que vemos uma bolsa de valores baseada em expectativas, probabilidades e decisões que movem o mundo. E essa inovação gigante tem uma brasileira no comando: Luana Lopes Lara, formada no MIT e agora parte da nova geração de bilionários construindo soluções do zero. O futuro dos mercados está mudando — e o Brasil está no mapa dessa transformação. 👉 Por que a Kalshi não é aposta, mesmo tendo eventos esportivos? 1) Porque é regulada como uma bolsa de derivativos A Kalshi tem licença federal da CFTC. Legalmente, ela funciona como um mercado financeiro, não como uma casa de apostas. 2) Porque o objetivo é econômico, não recreativo Os contratos servem para previsão, hedge e gestão de risco. A lógica é financeira, não de entretenimento. 3) Porque a estrutura é de exchange, não de “casa” Usuários negociam entre si; não existe “banca” lucrando contra o jogador, como ocorre em apostas tradicionais. E o resumo final pra ficar claro: *Mesmo com esportes, o que define aposta não é o tema — é a estrutura. E a estrutura da Kalshi é financeira. É um mercado, não um cassino. description: Stop scrolling! Is this investing or just high-stakes gambling? Prediction markets (like the CFTC-regulated Kalshi and crypto-native Polymarket) are booming, allowing people to trade contracts on future events like elections, sports, or macroeconomics. These markets claim to aggregate information efficiently, leveraging the "wisdom of the crowd". Historically, prediction markets, such as the Iowa Electronic Markets (IEM), have proven to be more accurate than traditional polls, particularly for long-term forecasts. Key platforms have distinct structures: • Kalshi is regulated as a financial exchange under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), operating legally in the US with high liquidity and offering interest on cash balances and open positions. • Polymarket is a decentralized prediction market, using USDC stablecoin, which has previously operated outside US regulatory approval (though recent legal movements suggest changes are coming). Advocates argue that success in these markets relies on skill, research, and finding arbitrage opportunities, differentiating it from games of pure chance. What do you think? description: Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA) pressed Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard on Wednesday on whether Iran posed an “imminent nuclear threat,” as the Trump administration has claimed in justifying its war against the regime.   Ms. Gabbard had skipped over a portion of her prepared opening statement before the Senate Intelligence Committee that stated Iran’s nuclear program had been “obliterated” by the U.S. strikes on the country’s underground facilities last June and that there had been “no efforts since then to try to rebuild their enrichment capacity.”   Sen. Ossoff read that portion during his questioning and asked whether it accurately reflected the intelligence community’s assessment, to which Ms. Gabbard said “yes.”   “The intelligence community assessed that Iran maintained the intention to rebuild and to continue to grow their nuclear enrichment capability,” she replied before Sen. Ossoff cut her off.   Sen. Ossoff repeated the question, prompting Ms. Gabbard to respond that the “only person who can determine what is and is not an imminent threat is the president.”   She said it was not the intelligence community’s responsibility to “determine what is and is not an imminent threat,” leaving Sen. Ossoff incredulous.   “It is precisely your responsibility to determine what constitutes a threat to the United States,” he said, before accusing her of “evading the question.” #jonossoff #tulsigabbard #iran #cspan

description: Is there going to be a draft? Are federal employees making money off of prediction markets? Did Iran bomb its own school? Are military leaders hoping for the rapture? It’s Misinformation Monday and I’m covering everything to do with Iran. Here’s more on prediction markets: Prediction markets, led by Kalshi and its chief competitor, Polymarket, are in the midst of an all-out sprint to turn almost every happening—from the world-moving to the mundane—into an online bet that can be won or lost.  Their surging popularity has sparked waves of concern over allegations of insider trading—and how speculators have hit it big on macabre wagers over war, death and crime.  Crypto-analytics firm Bubblemaps identified what it called “six suspected insiders” who made $1.2 million wagering that the U.S. would strike Iran last month. On Thursday, two Democratic senators, Amy Klobuchar and Jeff Merkley, introduced legislation to restrict federal officials from trading on prediction markets. Proponents say the markets don’t count as gambling, and that they harness the wisdom of crowds to accurately predict future events. Polymarket and Kalshi have recruited allies in high places, including Donald Trump Jr., who is an adviser to Kalshi and an investor in Polymarket.  As they attempt to build market share, both Kalshi and Polymarket have aimed marketing at an eager group of users that isn’t known for financial discretion: college students. Caption from article by Katherine Long, Kevin T. Dugan, Dana Mattioli and Angel Au-Yeung, Wall Street Journal.

description: Replying to @Mongi  This page shares educational stock market content based on historical price behavior, drawdowns, recoveries, and chart patterns. The goal is to make market history easier to understand by turning raw price action into simple, visual observations. Rather than focusing on hype, headlines, or short-term predictions, the content looks at how stocks have behaved over time through pullbacks, recoveries, and different market cycles. Each video is designed to break down past market behavior in a way that is clear, engaging, and grounded in data. The information comes from the NEXA algorithm, a rules-based system that scans historical stock price data. It looks at things like how often a stock has dropped by a certain amount, how long recoveries have taken, and how price behaved after similar setups in the past. NEXA does not predict the future. It is simply a tool used to organize historical market data and turn it into clear observations. Nothing shared here is financial advice, a recommendation, or a guarantee of future results. This content is for educational and informational purposes only. These posts are based on historical data, and market behavior can always change. NEXA is used to study what has happened before, not to tell anyone what they should do next. #stockanalysis #stocktok #aivideo #stocktips #amazon

description: Rwandan life in the 1950s was a blend of traditional culture and growing colonial influence, marked by significant political shifts under Belgian rule, increasing Westernization in fashion, and simmering ethnic tensions between Hutu and Tutsi groups, leading up to the Hutu Revolution of 1959, which upended the monarchy and forced many Tutsis to flee, transforming daily life and social structures towards eventual independence and conflict.  Since the import of Western clothing became popular in the 1950s, more Rwandans wore traditional clothing less often in their daily lives.  Cultural practices, including taboos (like milk and meat together) and strong respect for the monarchy (King Mutara), shaped daily life before the revolutionary changes.  The older ubuhake (clientage for cattle) and uburetwa (forced labor) systems were still present but challenged by new political dynamics.  In essence, the 1950s were a period of significant transition, as Rwanda moved from a traditional kingdom under colonial rule towards the precipice of independence, marked by deep social changes and the beginnings of profound conflict.

description: Gold is going down… and suddenly everyone is panicking. But this is where it gets interesting. When gold was rising, people were rushing in. Buying at higher prices, driven by hype, headlines, and FOMO. Now that it’s dropping? Those same people are selling. That’s not investing. That’s emotion. The market didn’t suddenly “break.” Interest rate expectations changed. Sentiment shifted. That’s what markets do. But here’s the truth most people don’t want to hear: Wealth isn’t built when everything feels safe. It’s built in uncertainty. Smart money doesn’t chase highs. It positions during fear. Short-term drops shake out weak hands. Long-term holders understand the bigger picture. Because zoom out for a second… Nothing about gold’s core value has changed. Inflation still exists. Debt still exists. Currency still loses purchasing power. So the real question is: Are you reacting… or are you positioning? #money #gold #news #war #richdadpoordad

description: It’s unclear whether US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, a former US Senator from Florida who ran against Trump in 2016 for the Republican presidential primaries, will seek the White House in 2028.  US President Donald Trump still has about 3 years remaining in his term — his second term, which makes it improbable he would run again unless he challenges the US constitution.  Potential successors are already jostling for position, and those include, on the Republican side, Vice President JD Vance and Rubio himself — who however already said he won’t run if Vance runs. Rubio, however, seems to have become Trump’s to advisor, always standing at his side.  Just yesterday, Trump was accompanied by Rubio as he was addressing the press before heading to Mar-a-Lago in Florida.  The President told reporters before their questions: “I though I bring our great Secretary of State out and he’s doing a fantastic job. So we have Marco.”  Rubio — who has been praised by a Trump numerous times this past year, including in his State of the Union address most recently — did not take the spotlight away from Trump as he was questioned by reporters on the South Lawn. He only briefly mention Cuba.  Meanwhile, prediction markets are paying attention to the top contenders, and it’s currently a three-horse race between Vance, Rubio, and, on the Democratic side, California Governor Gavin Newsom. According to betting platform Kalshi, Rubio is at 15% (up from 4% in October), Vance at 19% (down from 33% in October), and Newsom stable over time at 20%.  With two-and-a-half years before Election Day 2028, the upcoming 2026 midterm elections will offer a better picture on the next presidential race. As of now, the Democrats increasingly confident that they will take control of both the House — all but guaranteed by election betting odds — and the Senate.  This could kneecap Trump and his agenda and directly impact two key players in his administration, Vance and Rubio. #diplomacy #digitaldiplomacy
